title: Agent Inter-communication (A2A)
summary: Interoperate across independently operated agents through explicit capability discovery, task lifecycle contracts, authenticated messages, and verifiable artifacts.
overview: Agent inter-communication exchanges work requests and results across runtime or organizational boundaries. A useful contract specifies the requested task, identity, deadlines, accepted modalities, artifact schemas, and cancellation semantics. It does not require agents to expose their prompts, private reasoning, or internal orchestration implementation.

The Agent2Agent protocol provides a concrete interoperability model including Agent Cards, messages, tasks, and artifacts. Protocol versions evolve, so deployments should pin and negotiate supported versions rather than assume examples from different releases are interchangeable. Transport interoperability does not establish trust: advertised capabilities and returned artifacts still require independent validation.

production.poc: A prototype can call a known peer directly with a fixed contract. Verify that a remote agent adds a capability unavailable through an ordinary tool API.
production.production: Production introduces authenticated discovery, request signing or suitable transport security, scoped delegation, timeout rules, and stable correlation identifiers. Treat remote text and artifacts as untrusted input.
production.scale: At scale, capability registries, compatibility tests, and per-peer quotas become essential. Separate remote task status from local workflow status so a peer outage cannot silently turn an incomplete local operation into success.

components.name: Agent directory
components.role: Publishes trusted peer identities, supported contracts, and approved capability metadata.

components.name: Protocol adapter
components.role: Translates local task requests into the pinned peer protocol and normalizes responses.

components.name: Delegation policy
components.role: Limits which user authority and data can cross the peer boundary.

components.name: Remote task tracker
components.role: Maps local operations to remote task identifiers and lifecycle states.

components.name: Artifact verifier
components.role: Checks provenance, media type, schema, size, and safety before consuming remote results.

flow.title: Discover peer
flow.description: Resolve an approved identity and inspect its declared capabilities and protocol compatibility.

flow.title: Authorize delegation
flow.description: Confirm that the requester may share the required data and invoke the remote capability.

flow.title: Submit task
flow.description: Send bounded instructions, artifact references, deadline, and correlation metadata through an authenticated channel.

flow.title: Track lifecycle
flow.description: Observe streaming, polling, or callback updates according to the peer's supported capabilities.

flow.title: Validate artifact
flow.description: Verify returned evidence and distinguish completed work from requests for additional input.

flow.title: Close local task
flow.description: Record remote provenance, release resources, and reconcile cancellation or unknown outcomes.

diagrams.code:

 participant C as Carrier agent
 participant V as Artifact verifier
 L->>D: Resolve carrier capability and version
 D-->>L: Approved peer metadata
 L->>P: Check shipment data delegation
 P-->>L: Scoped authorization
 L->>C: Submit bounded routing task
 C-->>L: Remote task identifier
 L->>C: Read task progress
 C-->>L: Route artifact and evidence
 L->>V: Validate returned artifact

diagrams.caption: The local agent treats discovery, delegation, and artifact acceptance as separate trust decisions.

useCase.title: Coordinating a specialist carrier service
useCase.situation: A freight platform works with carriers whose routing expertise and operational systems remain under separate ownership.
useCase.problem: Custom integrations expose inconsistent task status and make it difficult to know whether a route proposal is final.
useCase.requirement: The assistant must request specialist routing evidence without disclosing unrelated customer records or losing task accountability.
useCase.architecture: A protocol adapter uses an approved carrier agent contract, scoped shipment data, and a local-to-remote task registry.
runtime: A dispatcher requests an alternative route; the platform discovers a compatible carrier capability and submits only the relevant shipment constraints.
The carrier returns a task identifier and later a route artifact, which is checked against dimensions, delivery windows, and approved endpoints.
useCase.failure: If the carrier becomes unreachable, the local task remains pending or expires explicitly; no booking is inferred from a missing response.
useCase.impact: Measure interoperability failures, remote task age, invalid artifacts, and peer-specific completion quality before expanding automated delegation.

tradeoffs.benefit: Reduces bespoke lifecycle integration between independent systems.
tradeoffs.cost: Version compatibility and profile differences still require testing.
Local operators have less visibility into remote failures.

tradeoffs.benefit: Long investigations can survive disconnected clients.
tradeoffs.cost: Status reconciliation and cancellation become distributed concerns.

failures.scenario: A malicious card advertises an internal endpoint
failures.detection: Discovery validation detects an unapproved host or identity.
failures.recovery: Reject the peer and investigate registry provenance.

failures.scenario: Remote success contains an invalid route
failures.detection: Artifact checks find violated shipment constraints.
failures.recovery: Reject the result and request correction without booking.

mistakes.fix: Apply explicit delegation policy for every task.
Share only the task data necessary for the peer capability.
Pin adapters and test supported lifecycle behavior.

whenToUse: Independent agent systems need a shared task lifecycle.
Partners must preserve their internal implementation boundaries.
Remote work requires artifacts and asynchronous progress.
whenNotToUse: A stable synchronous business API fully meets the requirement.
Peer identity and data-sharing authority cannot be established.
The integration does not need agent-specific task semantics.
checklist: Reconcile remote cancellation and unknown outcomes.
